name: Strahad Farsan
summary: Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan teaches warlocks to bind demons. The human warlock lives in a stone tower in the Barrens, beyond the reach of ordinary Alliance and Horde politics. Students of fel magic come from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity to learn from him.

sections.title: The Tower Above Ratchet
sections.body: Strahad Farsan keeps to a stone tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. The goblin port's neutral ground lets him practice dangerous summonings away from Alliance magistrates and Horde shamans. His acolytes gather around him as he studies the Twisting Nether, apart from the struggles over territory below.

sections.title: Master of Demonic Binding
sections.body: Strahad learned the danger of demonic binding firsthand. His first attempt to bind a felhunter nearly cost him his life, leaving him cautious and exacting. Despite being human, he has earned the respect of Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind and demonic scholars in the Undercity and Orgrimmar. Warlocks of either faction seeking to command felhunters or fiery steeds are sent to his tower.

faq.answer: Strahad Farsan teaches warlocks in a stone tower above Ratchet. He is part of the inner circle of Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind, and warlocks of both factions seek his skill in demonic summoning.

faq.q: Why is a human warlock living in the Barrens?
faq.answer: Strahad lives above Ratchet, a neutral port run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. The bluffs let him perform dangerous summoning rituals beyond the laws of the Alliance and the watch of the Horde.

faq.q: Why do Horde warlocks visit Strahad?
aliases: why do orcs go to strahad
faq.answer: Strahad's skill with demons draws warlocks from the Horde. Mentors in Orgrimmar and the Undercity recognize his knowledge of binding demons such as felhunters and send promising pupils across the sea to study with him.

faq.q: What happened to Strahad when he summoned his first felhunter?
faq.answer: Strahad's first attempt to bind a felhunter nearly cost him his life. He barely survived, and the ordeal taught him the precision needed to subdue such magic-consuming predators.

faq.q: Is Strahad related to Godrick Farsan?
faq.answer: Strahad and Godrick Farsan share the uncommon surname Farsan, which suggests a family connection. Strahad says nothing about family and remains devoted to his dark craft.

faq.q: Who are the acolytes around his tower?
faq.answer: Strahad's acolytes include Magaz, Fenrick, and Wytula. They help maintain protective wards, prepare summoning circles, and tend to the tower's rituals.

angles.text: As a warlock, you can learn from Strahad how to bind felhunters and summon steeds from the Nether.
Though born to the Alliance, Strahad deals with Horde practitioners in neutral Ratchet.
Gakin the Darkbinder sends Alliance warlocks from the crypts of the Slaughtered Lamb to Kalimdor to study under Strahad.
As a human, Strahad shows that masters of the dark arts seek greater power beyond Stormwind.
